transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-03-03
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Nina (Redwood), Ethan (CTO - SolsticePay), Priya (Head of ML), Jordan (SRE), Marta (PM)
Links shared: pricing-spreadsheet.xlsx, redwood-soc2-brief.pdf, pilot-benchmark-template.md

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:02] Ethan: yes loud and clear, thanks Maya.
[00:05] Maya: cool quick agenda — quick context on SolsticePay workloads, then Liam will walk through Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching and prefix / KV cache and then we'll go over cost model and pilot next steps.
[00:12] Priya: sounds good, our main constraint is p99 latency under 350ms for customer-facing flows and we do about ~600 QPS on peak bursts, but most is lower, and cost is obviously a huge factor.
[00:22] Maya: perfect that's exactly the kind of thing we've seen with other payments customers. Liam over to you.
[00:25] Liam: thanks, hi everyone, i'll share my screen — ok i'm pulling up the Optimize deck, micro note before i start: when we say batching here think of two layers — intra-request batching (consolidating multiple short prompts into a single GPU batch) and continuous batching at the runtime to maximize GPU utilization.
[00:40] Liam: so first slide, tradeoff overview: higher batch sizes improve throughput and lower cost per token but can increase tail latency. Redwood's runtime uses dynamic batching policy that adapts to SLO — you can set a target p99 and the runtime will prefer smaller batches to meet latency, but during idle periods it will pack more.
[00:58] Priya: that's helpful — do you have concrete numbers for e.g. 2048 context and 8k tokens? our flows average 120 tokens per request.
[01:05] Liam: yes for a 13B model on an A100-like instance, sample numbers: OPT-config with batch 1 p99 ~ 300ms, batch 8 p99 ~ 420ms but cost per token drops ~2.8x. those are illustrative — we run a quick pilot to measure on your traces. also quantization and kernel selection change these numbers.
[01:28] Jordan: when you say A100-like is that in dedicated or hosted? what's typical for Redwood Hosted?
[01:33] Maya: hosted generally runs on latest gen or equivalent; Dedicated lets you pick hardware and have predictability, which matters for financial firms with strict SLAs.
[01:42] Ethan: alignment to our compliance team — we may need private deployment or at least dedicated with VPC peering. how does caching impact data residency / retention?
[01:50] Liam: prefix caching (we often call prefix or prompt cache) doesn't store PII by default — it's a sequence-based cache that caches model KV states to speed repeated prefixes. KV cache is purely in-memory on the serving nodes; for Dedicated/Private you can configure TTLs and eviction policies and we integrate with customer KMS for logs and encryption-at-rest for any persisted artifacts. small note — some customers incorrectly call it KV cash in transcripts so you might see typos.
[02:18] Priya: ok so prefix cache would help our repeated flows like login prompts and TOS confirmations. do you have guidance on hit rates we should expect?
[02:24] Liam: yes typical hit rates for highly templated prompts are 30-60% depending on prompt variability; for payments confirmation flows we often see 45%+. higher hit rates reduce compute by avoiding repeated forward passes for prefix tokens.
[02:36] Liam: demo time — i'll show the cost model sheet: baseline hosted w/o caching + small batch = $X per 1M tokens, with KV cache hit 40% + batching = cost drops ~45%. (link posted).
[02:48] Maya: posted pricing spreadsheet in chat (pricing-spreadsheet.xlsx) and the security brief (redwood-soc2-brief.pdf).
[02:52] Ethan: quick question on complexity — how much engineering time to integrate the prefix caching path?
[02:56] Liam: on our SDKs it's a config flip for many customers — the runtime handles cache keys; for more customized caches you'd pass a stable conversation id. for private deployment we do a short integration with your SREs to ensure network/pinning. typical integration 1-2 sprints for production hardening.
[03:14] Priya: and what about cache invalidation for dynamic templates — e.g., tokens with per-request randomization?
[03:19] Liam: good question — you can choose cache scopes: strict prefix match, or more permissive with hashing only stable parts. when prompts have random nonce we recommend separating that piece as an input that isn't part of the prefix key. we can instrument hit vs miss dashboards in Console.
[03:33] Jordan: ok on the network side, we need to know whether the KV cache state remains solely in our VPC; if it's hosted, is the cache shared multi-tenant?
[03:41] Maya: hosted is multi-tenant service but customer inference data is siloed; the in-memory caches aren't exposed cross-tenant. for regulated workloads we'd recommend Dedicated or Private where you control the nodes.
[03:52] Ethan: what about cold-starts and warm-up when you spin new replicas? our traffic pattern scales up for BlackFriday-like events.
[03:57] Liam: we support pre-warming, pinned warm pools, and automatic warmup policies. Also KV cache warms faster for commonly used prefixes; for sudden spikes we can use a fallback lower-cost model variant to keep tail latency acceptable.
[04:12] Priya: variant fallback — is that automatic? any quality regression risk?
[04:15] Liam: you can configure automatic fallback to smaller models — Redwood Optimize simulates expected quality impact given your eval set; we recommend canarying fallbacks in the rollout.
[04:24] Maya: quick real example — for Meridian Payments we reduced token cost 52% using 40% KV cache hit + batching 4x. your mileage will vary.
[04:33] Ethan: nice. on encryption / audit logs — we need to show auditors that prompts were not persisted beyond X days. does Redwood keep prompt logs by default?
[04:41] Nina: we keep minimal telemetry for billing and performance; full prompt logs are off by default for hosted unless enabled. for Dedicated/Private, retention is configurable and can be routed to your log storage (S3 w/ encryption) and KMS.
[04:57] Marta: is there any known issue with caching and function calls or tool calling? we use external lookups in prompt building.
[05:03] Liam: function/tool calls usually happen post-generation; caching applies to prefix tokens only. if function outputs are part of the prompt by design, you'd scope caching accordingly and we recommend invalidation after tool execution.
[05:16] Priya: pilot idea — can we run a 1-week pilot with 10M tokens/day from our traffic replay to see hit rates and cost delta?
[05:22] Maya: absolutely — next steps we'll collect sample traces and you'll get a custom runbook. Liam will own the pilot plan.
[05:28] Liam: i'll outline the required artifacts: sample traces, QPS profile, example prompts, and a small eval set. we'll run bench on dedicated-like hardware and give a detailed cost-model.
[05:36] Jordan: on infra — we need to know required ports and whether we must open inbound to Redwood; we prefer VPC peering and private endpoint.
[05:42] Maya: heard — we'll share the network diagram and recommended firewall/IPs in the security pack.
[05:46] Ethan: any blockers from our side? compliance will review SOC2 and encryption docs.
[05:50] Nina: posted the SOC2 brief earlier, and we also have an architecture diagram — will send both.
[05:55] Priya: last technical thing — any data about cache TTL tuning? how often should we evict?
[06:00] Liam: recommendation: short-lived prefixes (auth flows) TTL 5-15 minutes; longer-lived (templated confirmations) 2-6 hours. eviction policies depend on memory footprint and hit patterns; we'll instrument and suggest values after pilot.
[06:12] Marta: ok, can you also include a cost sensitivity table that shows latency vs cost tradeoffs when adjusting batch size?
[06:18] Liam: yes that's in the spreadsheet — i'll add a column for p50/p95/p99 for each batch size and quantization option.
[06:24] Maya: recap / next steps: Maya to send pricing & security docs, Liam to send pilot plan and run benchmarks, Jordan to share VPC diagram and sample traces, target pilot start next week.
[06:34] Ethan: good summary, we'll get the artifacts over. thanks all.
[06:37] Maya: thanks folks, we'll follow up with proposed pilot dates.

End transcript.
Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., KV cash) and generic speaker tags. Audio quality medium but conversation complete.
